explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly compares LLM-as-a-judge against human evaluation using Cohen's kappa for agreement analysis, reporting quantitative metrics and discussing the relationship between methods

prompts.notes: Method adapted from original TruthfulQA paper but no exact prompts shown; judge models trained with learning rate 0.01 for 5 epochs

inter_annotator_agreement.value: similar between human evaluators and between humans and Judge-LLM

guidelines.notes: Human evaluation used binary labels (truthful/not-truthful, informative/not-informative); for long answers with additional claims, new information had to be fact-checked

sample_size.notes: 400 responses evaluated by both methods (100 questions each for 4 models across 5 languages); reliability measured on 50 overlapping manually-annotated responses per language

quantitative_scores.notes: English language, best performing Judge-LLM (Gemma 2 9B instruct trained with all MT data)

validation_results.summary_finding: LLM-as-a-Judge correlates more closely with human judgments than multiple-choice metrics across all languages, with Cohen's kappa agreements ranging from 0.60-0.75 for truthfulness and 0.78 for informativeness, showing higher correlation even when judge training data differs in format and language.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human evaluation assessed the same criteria on the same instances
